page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance within the Enhanced family, driven by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the configuration provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 48 MB of shared L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA-NI.

System memory is provisioned at 96.0 GB, establishing a substantial 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio suited for memory-bound tasks. In throughput testing, the memory subsystem achieves uncached read speeds of 78.47 GB/sec and write speeds of 52.52 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are absent, and the instance carries no integrated local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for stateful data retention. Network baseline performance is rated at 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.r7t.3xlarge largely within expected mid-tier ranges, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 1599.0, a multi-core score of 7867.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 16516.22. In in-memory data processing, the instance logged 11.97 million Redis SET operations per second and handled PassMark database operations at 5826.28. While smaller LLM inference workloads run effectively, larger models show diminished performance, with 7B parameter prompt processing dropping into the lower quartile at 24.29 tokens per second due to CPU-only execution constraints.

The qualitative cost profile is characterized by high memory density per compute core, offering efficiency for environments requiring large working sets without paying for unneeded vCPUs. Tradeoffs include the total reliance on remote storage fabrics for disk operations and modest vector throughput for large language models. The ecs.r7t.3xlarge is appropriate for in-memory caches, relational database systems, enterprise ERP backends, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines.

Engineered for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, it delivers an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio alongside an 8 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance includes 48 MB of L3 cache, hardware cryptographic acceleration, and AVX-512 instruction support, though it lacks local disk storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network block storage for persistence. Performance benchmarks place the instance in mid-range tiers across general compute, recording 11.97 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 78.47 GB/sec in large-block memory read bandwidth. While larger AI model inferencing is constrained by CPU execution, the high memory density delivers solid operational efficiency for in-memory databases, Redis caches, mid-scale relational database engines, and analytics workloads that demand large in-memory capacities.
